author: Rachel Estrada
title: Houston Port seizes $6M in FIFA 2026 World Cup fake merchandise - NewsBreak
text:
By Rachel Estrada ,
2 hours ago
Editor’s Note: Above video is of Kirby at Houston Zoo in Summer of Soccer spirit
HOUSTON (CW39) – Federal officers at the Houston seaport said Wednesday that they have seized more than $6 million worth of counterfeit merchandise tied to FIFA World Cup 2026 trademarks, including thousands of soccer jerseys, soccer balls, shoes, toys, perfumes and fake Apple products, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP).
The bust comes as officials continue monitoring shipments linked to major sporting events and growing e-commerce activity. The Department of Homeland Security said Wednesday the operation targeted shipments violating intellectual property rights connected to FIFA World Cup 2026 branding and merchandise.
What did CBP seize in Houston? The largest portion of the seizure included sports merchandise connected to FIFA World Cup 2026 trademarks. CBP officers confiscated approximately 12,000 fake Adidas soccer jerseys and 4,500 fake Adidas FIFA soccer balls. Officers also seized nearly 4,400 fake pairs of athletic shoes.
The operation uncovered additional shipments containing toys, perfumes and 69 fake FIFA-related packages carrying more than 2,200 counterfeit Apple watches and earbuds displaying fake FIFA trademarks. Taken together, officials said the merchandise carried a domestic value exceeding $6 million.
Why was the operation conducted now? CBP said the operation was part of ongoing enforcement ahead of major events like the FIFA World Cup. The agency targeted shipments suspected of violating FIFA trademarks and copyrights. Most of the seized shipments originated in China and were headed to destinations in and outside the United States.
How do counterfeit products impact consumers? CBP officials say counterfeit goods often appear legitimate at first glance but may fall short in quality and safety.
CBP takes very seriously our role in protecting American consumers from low quality and potentially dangerous counterfeit items. Unfortunately, these criminal networks are very deceptive in scamming sports fans and harming American consumers and businesses.
CBP Area Port Director Thomas Mahn Officials said counterfeit products can impact businesses that legally own trademarks while also creating risks for consumers who think they are purchasing genuine merchandise.
What types of products are commonly counterfeited? CBP says counterfeiters target more than sports merchandise, including medications, cosmetics, toys, fashion items, electronics and auto parts. Officials warn some fake products may pose health and safety risks. More than 90% of counterfeit seizures occur in international mail and express shipments tied to e-commerce.
What should shoppers know before buying online? CBP is encouraging consumers to purchase products from reputable online sources and to be cautious when deals appear unusually attractive. Before purchasing jerseys, electronics or event-related merchandise online, verify the seller and product source. A lower price may look appealing, but knowing where a product comes from can help protect both your wallet and your safety.
